feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It reads professionally, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and strategic scope over time.  
- Good use of scale indicators and concrete platforms/tools (10,000+ pages, 3.5M page views, GA4, Drupal, BigQuery), which boosts credibility.  
- Strong positioning for digital transformation, governance, analytics, and multimedia leadership in mission-driven organizations.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Header, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Footer/Projects; consolidate to create a tighter, more scannable structure.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions: e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption rates, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; maintain consistent punctuation in bullets; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization may feel inconsistent unless intentional branding.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector focus. However, it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, and would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one concise value proposition plus one evidence-based sentence; add scale where possible.
- Replace generic “leads” phrasing with outcome-oriented language tied to enterprise platforms and communications operations.
- Reduce the list of capabilities already covered in Core Competencies; keep only the most differentiating themes.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Combines digital strategy, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, and multimedia production to improve how complex, mission-driven organizations publish, measure, and scale audience-facing communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies, Recent Projects, and Topline Skills.
- The subtitle already signals leadership; avoid restating a long capability list in the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize strategic capability areas rather than repeating detailed skill phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use broader, executive-level categories: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and performance optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership
- Keep the most distinctive strengths tied to recent work: AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style by replacing “&” with “and” for consistency across the CV
- Consider reducing to 6–7 items to improve scanability and avoid reading like a second skills list

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search” repeat Topline Skills/Technical + IT almost verbatim
- “Enterprise website modernization” and “digital governance/editorial systems” are already stated clearly in the header summary
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots that reinforce the headline, but the block is text-dense and overlaps with work experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a simple lead-in and convert to cleaner bullets for scanability; keep each project to one line.
- Use parallel verbs and tighter phrasing: “Created,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched.”
- Add one concrete result, audience, or scale detail where possible; otherwise trim feature lists.
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled,” “10 x 20-foot,” and consistent comma usage.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI Hybrid Search,” the microsite, and the video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in the current freelance and NACo roles.
- Consider positioning this as “Selected Projects” with only the most distinctive examples, or swap in projects not already described in work experience.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the opening, foreground outcomes, and avoid repeating project details already covered in Recent Projects and prior NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with a sharper value statement: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, enterprise web improvement, and content operations for coordinated, multi-channel communications.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with verbs like “Built,” “Led,” “Improved,” “Advised.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users, publishers, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search relevance gains, or reduction in publishing friction.
- Example rewrite: “Led development of AI-enabled search, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX to improve access to complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal microsite structures,” “AI-enabled search,” and campaign storytelling duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the specifics.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize what is new or more advanced in this consulting work.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if the opening is tighter, outcomes are more explicit, and channel-management language is reduced to avoid overlap with earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/result summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Recast bullets to emphasize enterprise outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for studio/analytics/governance work: cost savings, faster reporting, improved publishing consistency, reduced vendor reliance, increased production volume, or stronger engagement.
- Tighten channel bullet: focus on ownership and scale, not generic management, e.g., “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on transformation, infrastructure, and leadership.
- Video production language may duplicate older NACo roles unless framed as building the in-house studio capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Tighten it to emphasize scope growth, cross-functional coordination, and channel-building contributions specific to 2018–2022.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to show ownership and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Make bullets more outcome-focused: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video bullet: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets for concision: “Improved editorial planning and digital publishing workflows, strengthening coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” closely repeat the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership scope and distinct value rather than broad communications phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector stakeholder communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Executive advisory on digital communications” if you want a more senior, recent emphasis.
- Keep phrasing parallel: use noun phrases only, avoid mixing “messaging” with “planning” and “leadership.”
- If space allows, add one qualifier tied to scale, e.g. “enterprise web and content governance.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat language already used in the header and core competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo roles; avoid repeating advocacy unless it is a target-role keyword.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, not a software inventory.
- Prioritize recent strengths tied to current/most recent roles: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI search, integrations, automation.
- Trim older/lower-signal items unless job-relevant; move detailed tools to Technical + IT.

Suggested edit:
- Drupal platform leadership
- CMS modernization and migration
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- Airtable-based content systems
- AI-enabled search and discovery experiences

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current list duplicates Technical + IT almost line-for-line; avoid repeating WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, jQuery here unless essential for the target role.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; consider keeping it in one place only.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making and optimization outcomes, not just tool names.

Suggested edit
- Reframe as a concise capability line: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity for analytics infrastructure, KPI design, executive reporting and performance optimization.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive dashboards/reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with “SEO, UX and conversion/performance analysis” only if those areas are supported elsewhere.
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “used to support strategic decisions” or “used to guide content and platform improvements.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid listing the same tools in three places unless this section adds a stronger strategic angle than the technical list.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skills item is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Make it tighter, more senior, and aligned to recent leadership-level multimedia/event delivery rather than hands-on task lists alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for scope and level: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows • Virtual event production”
- If you want stronger leadership positioning, use: “Multimedia production leadership • Livestream and hybrid event operations • Studio buildout and management • PTZ/multi-camera systems • Virtual event delivery”
- Replace “video production and editing” with a broader phrase unless editing is a key differentiator; tools already appear in Technical + IT.
- Keep to 4–5 terms max and order by strategic value: livestream/hybrid events and studio operations should come before equipment-specific skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; consider varying this item’s wording to avoid repetition.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” are close; combine if space is tight.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise content platforms, migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize strongest/recent tools first: Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Consider adding level/context instead of just names, e.g., “Drupal (advanced), WordPress (working), SharePoint (working)” if accurate
- If Drupal is the clear flagship, you could shorten further to: Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” under Topline Skills; consider removing one version or making this one more tool-only and the other more capability-focused.
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear elsewhere, so don’t add them here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more implementation-focused and selective so it supports recent hands-on work without repeating broader skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML5/CSS3, JavaScript, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.” Consider dropping jQuery unless it is still actively used in recent work.
- If space allows, add scope/context instead of just tools: “Front-end development, API integrations, tag management, edge scripting, and deployment automation.”
- If these were used recently, align to current projects: mention “Drupal front-end implementation,” “campaign microsites,” or “deployment workflows” to connect with 2022–present experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations.”
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap conceptually with “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills; keep it here only if emphasizing technical CI/CD.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize automation/integration tools over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Project Systems
- Reorder by relevance/strength: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana
- Move collaboration tools out unless central to workflow design; if kept, group them last: Slack • Teams
- Consider adding function labels for clarity: Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (process automation) • Jira/Asana (project workflows)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Basecamp and Trello may dilute the section if they were not meaningful parts of recent, higher-impact work.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay concise and tool-focused rather than implying broad channel ownership again.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform names for readability and consistency: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one qualifier to show level of use without repeating work history, e.g. “enterprise newsletter and member communications platforms”
- Keep it as a platform list only; avoid adding verbs like “managed” or “led” here since those are better covered in recent experience bullets

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications” and newsletter leadership are already covered in Core Competencies and NACo experience; don’t restate them here
- If Higher Logic was the primary email/member platform at NACo, consider listing the most relevant platform first to match recent experience

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to signal level of use or business impact. Tighten it into a more capability-led line and avoid generic filler.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI • Analytics implementation and KPI reporting • SEO analysis • Experimentation/A/B testing
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI reporting” or “Executive dashboards” to sound more outcome-oriented.
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses for strongest tools, e.g., “GA4 (enterprise reporting), BigQuery (data pipelines), Power BI/Looker Studio (executive dashboards).”
- Keep only tools and higher-value capabilities; avoid broad terms that are already proven in recent NACo experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item is nearly identical to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider removing one or making this version more technical/tool-specific.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so don’t repeat them elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, web refresh support, and multimedia production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution, not generic support: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve publishing workflows across web, email, social, and video.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or process improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while informally supervising a digital media associate.”
- If accurate, use stronger verbs like “launched,” “streamlined,” “produced,” and “trained” instead of “contributed” and “provided guidance.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early production rather than expansion.
- “strengthening workflows” overlaps with later governance/operations bullets; keep this item at a more tactical, hands-on level.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting NACo programs and policy initiatives.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Condense the remaining media work into one clear phrase: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support organizational communications and member engagement.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this broader and more foundational.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language here since those strengths are better established in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skills, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. Make it more tool-focused and concise, with only the most relevant production capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia Tools
- Tighten content to: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production workflows • Podcast editing/production
- Use parallel phrasing: list software first, then production capabilities; avoid mixing broad functions with tools inconsistently.
- If accurate, add one stronger differentiator instead of a generic term, e.g. “Broadcast studio production” or “Multi-camera livestream production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with Topline Skills (“Livestreaming,” “Studio operations,” “Hybrid and virtual event production”); keep only one version.
- “Podcast production” is already supported by older experience; retain it only if you want to signal continued relevance.
